newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW to keep plants at work during summer.
newsitem.headline: VW to keep plants at work during summer.

text.p: Forget about a lazy summer holiday at German carmaker Volkswagen AG.
Volkswagen and Audi AG, its luxury carmaker unit, have announced special shifts during August, and even through the rest of the year, in a bid to reduce delivery times for popular models.
Audi said on Tuesday it would maintain almost half of its vehicle production during the first three weeks of August -- usually time for a company holiday when factories are shut.
Audi said it would build about 800 to 1,000 of its popular A3 and A4 models at its Ingolstadt plant compared with regular production of about 1,600 models per day.
At its plant in Neckarsulm, Audi said it would build from 300 to 550 of its A6, cabrio and A8 models compared with regular daily production of 530 vehicles.

VW said on Monday it would introduce a total of 30 special shifts at its Wolfsburg plant to speed up production of its Golf and Polo models as well as for the Seat Arosa model, which is also made at the plant in the carmaker's hometown.

A buyer of a Golf model, which will be replaced this fall with a new model to be unveiled at the Frankfurt car show, has to wait about six to eight weeks, while buyers of a Polo or Arosa model must wait up to 12 weeks.
Each special shift allows production on that day to be increased by about 50 percent. In a normal day about 1,300 Golfs, 400 Polos and 250 Seat Arosas are made at that plant.
Other carmakers, including BMW AG, at the moment said they were not planning additional shifts during the summer holiday period.
